lessons.title: Your 90-day support improvement plan and next steps
objectives: Assemble the final capstone portfolio
Write a 90-day plan with a specific tracking system or skill and measurable targets
Set realistic targets using your own baseline metrics
Choose next learning steps to grow in customer support

blocks.text: You have built a complete support toolkit: a set-up WhatsApp Business account, templates, a safety kit, a tracking sheet, policies and FAQs, metrics and a portfolio. This final lesson helps you turn it into a plan for the next 90 days, so the skills grow instead of fading, and prepares you for the course capstone and certificate.

blocks.name: certification
blocks.caption: Your certificate is backed by a portfolio that proves what you can do.

blocks.text: Start from your baseline

A **baseline** is where you are now. Before setting targets, look at your current numbers from your tracking sheet: average FRT, resolution rate, FCR and CSAT, plus the number of tickets. Targets should improve on your own baseline, step by step, rather than copy a number from somewhere else.

blocks.title: Worked example: setting realistic targets
blocks.context: For example, Uche's baseline over 2 weeks: 130 tickets, average FRT 45 minutes, resolution rate 82%, CSAT 78% from 50 responses.
steps: FRT: she sees most slow replies happen between 12 pm and 2 pm when she is also packing orders. Target: average FRT under 30 minutes by day 60, by checking chats every 30 minutes and using quick replies.
Resolution rate: 82% means 18 of every 100 tickets were left open. Target: 90% by day 90, by reviewing "Waiting for us" at 5 pm daily.
CSAT: target 85% by day 90, by adding a follow-up message after deliveries.
Change in FRT: (45 − 30) ÷ 45 × 100 ≈ 33% faster.
She plans to measure every 2 weeks using the same sheet and the same rules.
blocks.result: Uche's targets are specific, based on her own data, and each is linked to one concrete action.

blocks.title: A 90-day plan in three stages
items: Days 1-30: baseline and fixes
Days 31-60: build new habit
Days 61-90: measure and report
blocks.caption: Each stage ends with a short check of your metrics.

blocks.text: What a good 90-day plan includes

items: **One tracking system:** for example "move from ad-hoc chats to the 10-column Google Sheet for every ticket" or "set up a Freshdesk free plan and route the support email into it".
**One skill to build:** for example de-escalation writing, typing speed, or spreadsheet formulas.
**Two or three targets** based on your baseline, with dates.
**Specific actions** that will move each target.
**Review dates:** every 2 weeks, with a short note of what changed.

head: Day
Action
Measure
rows: 1 to 7
Log every ticket in the sheet; record baseline
Ticket count, FRT, resolution rate
8 to 30
Add 5 new quick replies from top categories; publish 3 FAQs
Repeat questions per week
Daily 5 pm review of open tickets; follow-up message after delivery
Resolution rate, CSAT
Write 2-weekly reports; update portfolio with a new case
All metrics against baseline

blocks.text: Common mistakes in 90-day plans

items: **Too many goals.** Three targets you achieve are worth more than ten you forget. Pick the ones that matter most to customers.
**Targets without actions.** "CSAT 90%" is a wish. "Send a follow-up message after every delivery to raise CSAT from 78% to 85%" is a plan.
**Changing the rules midway.** If you start counting FRT only during working hours, keep that rule for all 90 days, or your comparison will mislead you.
**No review dates.** Without a calendar reminder, most plans stop after two weeks.
**Ignoring wellbeing.** Faster replies should come from better tools and habits, not from answering chats at midnight. Keep your working hours and away message.

blocks.text: Finishing your capstone

items: Gather your three documented interactions from Lesson 4.1, including one challenging case.
Check each has your exact replies and your reasoning for each step.
Add your evidence pack: quick replies, tracking sheet, metrics and a weekly report.
Write your 90-day plan naming your tracking system or skill, targets and review dates.
Anonymise everything, save as one PDF, and submit it.

blocks.text: Next learning steps

To keep growing, consider free courses from help-desk and customer-experience companies, for example **HubSpot Academy**, and the help centres of tools such as Freshdesk and Zoho Desk, which explain features like automations and knowledge bases. Practise spreadsheet skills: pivot tables let you count tickets by category in seconds. As you gain experience, support roles can lead to team lead, quality assurance, customer success and operations positions.

blocks.title: Keep your portfolio alive
blocks.text: Add a new case every month and update your metrics. A portfolio with recent dates shows that your skills are current.

blocks.title: Share what you learned
blocks.text: Teach one thing from this course to someone else, for example how to set up quick replies. Explaining it is one of the best ways to make sure you really understand it.

takeaways: Set targets from your own baseline, not borrowed numbers.
Your 90-day plan needs one system, one skill, targets, actions and review dates.
Measure every 2 weeks with the same rules.
Your capstone combines three cases, evidence and the 90-day plan.

activity.title: Write your 90-day plan
steps: Record your baseline metrics from your tracking sheet.
Choose one tracking system and one skill to build.
Set two or three dated targets, each with an action.
Fill in a day-by-day table like the one in this lesson.
Put review dates in your phone calendar.
activity.evidence: Your written 90-day plan with baseline, targets, actions and review dates.

quiz.q: Which set of three portfolio cases shows the widest range of skills?
options: A routine request, a problem solved through the workflow, and a challenging interaction
quiz.explain: Different case types show efficiency, problem solving and de-escalation.

quiz.q: What must you do before putting a real customer chat in your portfolio?
options: Nothing, if the customer was rude
Remove names, numbers, addresses and order details that identify the customer
Add the customer's phone so employers can verify
Post it on your status first
quiz.explain: Anonymising protects the customer's personal data.

quiz.q: A remote job offer asks you to pay ₦15,000 for "training materials" before you start. What should you do?
options: Pay quickly to secure the job
Treat it as a warning sign, do not pay, and check the company
Share your BVN to prove identity
Ask them to reduce the fee
quiz.explain: Genuine employers pay you. Upfront fees are a common recruitment scam sign.

quiz.q: Which CV line is strongest?
options: "Handled about 60 tickets per week; average FRT 20 minutes; 90% resolution rate"
quiz.explain: Specific, measurable achievements you can back up are most convincing.

quiz.q: Ola's average FRT drops from 40 minutes to 30 minutes. By what percentage did it improve?
What should a 90-day target be based on?
options: Your own baseline from your tracking sheet
quiz.explain: Targets based on your own data are realistic and measurable.

quiz.q: In the STAR interview structure, what does the A stand for?
quiz.explain: STAR is Situation, Task, Action, Result.

finalQuiz.q: Which channel is best for confirming the details of a ₦40,000 refund?
options: A written record such as email or the logged chat, after owner approval
finalQuiz.explain: Money matters need written, findable records and the right approval (Module 1).

finalQuiz.q: What do greeting and away messages on WhatsApp Business mainly do?
options: Set honest expectations about who you are and when you reply
finalQuiz.explain: They set expectations; they do not count as a human first response (Modules 1 and 3).

finalQuiz.q: A customer asks you to send them "the code that just came to your phone". What should you do?
options: Refuse; never share verification codes or OTPs
Ask the owner to send it
finalQuiz.explain: Sharing a verification code can let someone take over the account (Module 1).

finalQuiz.q: What are the six steps of the support workflow in order?
options: Log, solve, acknowledge, check, clarify, confirm
Acknowledge, clarify, check, solve or escalate, confirm, log
Solve, thank, log, clarify, check, confirm
Clarify, acknowledge, log, confirm, check, solve
finalQuiz.explain: Acknowledge, clarify, check, solve or escalate, confirm, log (Module 2).

finalQuiz.q: Which reply follows the recommended structure best?
options: "Hello Amina, sorry it is late. Your parcel will arrive Thursday before 4 pm; the rider will call first. Thank you for your patience."
"Not our fault, the rider is slow."
finalQuiz.explain: It greets, acknowledges, answers with a specific time, gives the next step and closes warmly (Module 2).

finalQuiz.q: A furious customer accuses the shop of scamming her. Using LAST, what should your first reply do?
options: Restate her problem to show you listened and apologise sincerely
finalQuiz.explain: Listen and Apologise come before Solve and Thank (Module 2).

finalQuiz.q: Which columns are essential in a ticket sheet for calculating first response time?
options: Time received and first reply time
finalQuiz.explain: FRT = first reply time minus time received (Module 3).

finalQuiz.q: Seven tickets had FRTs of 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30 and 35 minutes. What is the average?
A team received 200 tickets and resolved 170. Of the resolved ones, 102 were solved in the first reply. What are the resolution rate and FCR?
Out of 50 rating responses, 30 gave 5, 10 gave 4, 6 gave 3 and 4 gave 2. What is CSAT if 4 and 5 count as satisfied?
A customer reports illness after eating a snack the business sells. What is correct?
options: Advise stopping use and seeking medical help, collect batch details, escalate to the owner the same day
finalQuiz.explain: Safety complaints are High priority; agents do not give medical advice (Module 3).

finalQuiz.q: Which is a warning sign of a remote job scam?
options: A fee required before you can start
finalQuiz.explain: Genuine employers do not charge you to work (Module 4).
